week_in_brief: Patients are getting medical advice from free AI tools faster than you can schedule them an appointment.

items.headline: Your Patients Are Already Using AI—Just Not Yours
items.whats_happening: Nearly 60% of consumers are now using generative AI tools like ChatGPT and Google Gemini for symptom checking and test-result interpretation before they contact providers, according to Boston Consulting Group's 13,000-person survey. They're doing this because your digital front door is slower and less helpful. The risk isn't just that patients are getting unregulated advice—it's that they're forming care decisions before you're even in the conversation.
items.so_what: If your system doesn't offer a trusted, proprietary AI tool for triage or health questions, patients will keep using free consumer tools instead. You lose the engagement moment, and worse—you lose the chance to direct them to the right care pathway.

items.headline: Compliance Gaps in AI Marketing Are Drawing Federal Heat
items.whats_happening: MEDVi, an AI-powered telehealth company, just got hit with FDA warnings and FTC investigations for using AI-generated physician personas with fake credentials and unsubstantiated weight-loss claims. The bigger issue: AI-driven marketing for healthcare is far less regulated than clinical AI tools, so enforcement falls to general consumer-protection law. The FTC is making it clear that you're responsible for what your affiliate networks and paid-media vendors say on your behalf.
items.so_what: Audit your third-party vendors and affiliate marketing partners now. If they're using AI to generate claims, creative, or targeting—and you haven't reviewed the output—you own the compliance risk.

items.headline: The HIPAA Security Rule Is About to Get Stricter
items.whats_happening: Proposed updates to the HIPAA Security Rule eliminate the distinction between "addressable" and "required" safeguards, meaning compliance will become more prescriptive with less room for organizational judgment. Layer in new CMS mandates, state privacy laws, and AI governance rules, and the old compliance playbook—spreadsheets, email chains, quarterly audits—won't cut it anymore. Final rule expected this year.
items.so_what: Start aligning your safeguard inventory to the new framework now, and evaluate whether your current compliance-tech stack can handle tighter requirements. Waiting for the final rule means catching up under pressure.

items.headline: Google's Paid Search Is Starting to Work Like SEO
items.whats_happening: Google is shifting paid search away from strict keyword targeting toward intent-based signals that prioritize creative relevance and user context. AI Overviews are now citing pages beyond the top 10 results, meaning paid and organic search increasingly depend on the same authority signals. Average CPC is $5.26, and weak landing pages or generic ad copy are getting punished faster than before.
items.so_what: Your paid search strategy now needs to align with your SEO and content strategy. If your landing pages don't reflect real authority or clear messaging, you're wasting budget on both sides.

this_weeks_take: The gap between what patients expect and what health systems deliver is widening. Consumers want AI tools, real-time availability, and frictionless digital experiences—and they're getting it from non-healthcare companies. If you're not competing on speed and experience, you're not competing at all.
